verdicts.summary: An approved factor B inhibitor is an attractive route, but the protective loss-of-function signal and the red safety light make this a cautious first test.

reasons.text: A loss-of-function CFB variant that looks protective argues against inhibition, and a red safety light is not outweighed by a large epithelial rise; the test should read epithelial damage, as proposed.
reasons.claim: a CFB loss-of-function variant linked to perianal Crohn's disease implies its function protects

verdicts.summary: Neutrophil chemokine with a clean safety profile, but redundant CXCR2 ligands and a bulk rise that mostly reflects neutrophil influx make single-ligand blockade uncertain.

reasons.text: Only 13% of the bulk rise is kept after composition adjustment and the protein is not quantified, so the claim that blocking corrects a change of the tissue is not supported by the card.
reasons.claim: most of its bulk rise is explained by cell proportions

verdicts.summary: A clean epithelial change with no functional, genetic or mouse evidence and no extracellular part; a reasonable organoid screen, not yet a target.

reasons.text: Intrinsic epithelial rise and clean safety support a first knockdown, but with no paper beyond a list mention the case rests on expression alone.
reasons.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence

verdicts.summary: A strong marker, but the knockout mouse develops more severe colitis, so inhibiting it may harm the epithelium.

reasons.text: Chi3l1 knockout mice developed severe colitis under AOM/DSS, with fewer tumours, so blockade may impair epithelial protection while limiting cancer.
reasons.claim: so blocking it could harm the epithelium
reasons.quote: Here we demonstrate that CHI3L1 (aka Brp39) knockout (KO) mice treated with azoxymethane (AOM)/dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) developed severe colitis but lesser incidence of CAC as compared to that in wild-type (WT) mice.

verdicts.summary: A stromal secreted protease with a retained rise and clean safety, but one expression paper and no function, genetics or mouse data.

reasons.text: The change survives adjustment and is already up in non-inflamed mucosa, but the biology of the protease in colitis is unknown, so the first experiment is exploratory.
reasons.claim: its literature is one expression paper

verdicts.summary: A ubiquitous mitochondrial gene with one instrument, no change in biopsies and a predicted cell that differs from the single-cell one; not a first-year target.

reasons.text: Biopsies show a slight fall rather than a rise, the predicted and observed cells disagree, and a mitochondrial elongation factor cannot be inhibited selectively; the genetic signal is a hypothesis about one cell type.
reasons.claim: which does not support the inhibition hypothesis in tissue

verdicts.summary: The best-supported case in the pool, with two mouse knockdown studies, but cancer biology is unsettled and both studies are recent and unreplicated.

reasons.text: Epithelial, intrinsic and functionally supported, but described as a tumour suppressor, so long-term inhibition needs an explicit cancer read-out alongside the organoid test.
reasons.claim: so its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled

verdicts.summary: A secreted BMP antagonist with a stromal rise only partly retained, an unsettled producing cell and no functional or mouse data.

reasons.text: Only 28% of the bulk rise is kept and the in-situ signal sits in smooth muscle, so the cell for the first experiment is uncertain; restoring BMP activity could also matter for epithelium.
reasons.claim: so the producing cell is not settled

verdicts.summary: A local-inflammation signal with null genetics, a known safety event and a negative antibody result in experimental colitis.

reasons.text: The card itself shows a null genetic test, a negative animal antibody result and an amber safety light; an approved drug alone does not justify the first slot.
reasons.claim: an anti-P-selectin antibody did not significantly improve colitis

verdicts.summary: TLR4/MD-2 blockade helps in mouse colitis models but one antibody impaired mucosal healing, and the gene is largely a neutrophil signal.

reasons.text: Mixed mouse results (benefit early, impaired healing in recovery) and a neutrophil-arrival signal argue for reading both phases in the explant test, as the card proposes.
reasons.claim: another anti-TLR4/MD-2 antibody interfered with mucosal healing during recovery

verdicts.summary: Activin blockade has support in mouse colitis, but the gene is strongly constrained and the cell and replication across atlases are weak.

reasons.text: Follistatin, which neutralises activins, reduced histologic score and myeloperoxidase activity in TNBS and DSS colitis and in IL-10-deficient mice, supporting activin blockade.
reasons.claim: administration of follistatin attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration
reasons.quote: Administration of follistatin also reduced the histologic score and tissue myeloperoxidase activity in established TNBS and DSS colitis and reduced the severity of the colitis in IL-10 -/- mice.

reasons.text: A LOEUF of 0.17 and a lineage that does not replicate in any other atlas weigh against it; sotatercept is a ligand trap acting on several activins, not on INHBA alone.

verdicts.summary: A broadly expressed myeloid transcription factor whose predicted cell is not its main source and whose genetic test points the other way.

reasons.text: The predicted dendritic cell is not the main source, Mendelian randomisation does not agree, and a transcription factor expressed in neutrophils and macrophages would be hard to inhibit selectively.
reasons.claim: the predicted dendritic cell is not the main source

verdicts.summary: A fine-mapped signal with a small predicted effect in NK cells, no Mendelian support and no change in biopsies.

reasons.text: Every layer beyond the sequence prediction is null or absent; it is an inherited-risk hypothesis, not a first-year treatment target.
reasons.claim: Mendelian randomisation gives no support, and biopsies show no change

verdicts.summary: A small predicted expression effect with no Mendelian support and no change in biopsies.

reasons.text: Only the sequence prediction supports it, so confirming the variant effect is a prerequisite, not a target test.
reasons.claim: no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies

verdicts.summary: An intrinsic epithelial rise in a crypt zone that may be a repair programme, with no functional or genetic evidence.

reasons.text: The card flags a possible repair programme; inhibiting it could impair healing, so the wound-healing arm of the experiment is essential and the gene is a screen, not a target.
reasons.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence

verdicts.summary: A biomarker-supported regeneration gene; blocking it could slow repair and there is no functional study in either direction.

reasons.text: Crypt-zone rise with a repair programme flag and only biomarker papers; restoring rather than blocking may be the direction, which the organoid test with protein addition addresses.
reasons.claim: so blocking it could slow repair

objections.claim: knockout mice are protected from colitis
objections.objection: The knockout study cited on the card reports the opposite: Chi3l1-null mice developed severe colitis, with fewer tumours. The text contradicts itself, since protection would not imply harm to the epithelium.
objections.suggestion: Say that knockout mice develop more severe colitis but less colitis-associated cancer, so blocking it could harm the epithelium.
objections.quote: Here we demonstrate that CHI3L1 (aka Brp39) knockout (KO) mice treated with azoxymethane (AOM)/dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) developed severe colitis but lesser incidence of CAC as compared to that in wild-type (WT) mice.

objections.claim: an inhibitor was approved for UC and was never tried in UC
objections.objection: Self-contradictory, and the card shows the inhibitor is in phase 3 for sepsis, not approved for UC.
objections.suggestion: Say that an inhibitor reached phase 3 for sepsis and was never tried in UC.

objections.claim: higher expression in sigmoid colon lowers UC risk
objections.objection: An odds ratio per SD of 1.191 means higher expression raises risk, as the summary and the risk allele in the same card say. The sentence contradicts them.
objections.suggestion: Say that higher expression in sigmoid colon raises UC risk.

objections.claim: UniProt describes it as an oncogene
objections.objection: The SERPINB5 card says UniProt describes it as a tumour suppressor; the summary says the opposite.
objections.suggestion: Say that UniProt describes it as a tumour suppressor, while a study of IBD tissue linked its aberrant expression with neoplastic transformation.

objections.claim: most of its bulk rise is explained by cell proportions, so blocking it would correct a change of the tissue itself
objections.objection: Only 13% of the bulk rise is kept after adjustment, which means it is largely neutrophil arrival; the conclusion that blocking corrects a change of the tissue does not follow.
objections.suggestion: Say that most of its bulk rise is explained by cell proportions, so it reports neutrophil influx in part.
